option_relations.rationale: Viral cardiomyopathy is a type of infectious myocarditis, where a viral infection leads to inflammation of the heart muscle.
Fulminant myocarditis is a severe and rapidly progressive form of myocarditis, which can be caused by infections.

Myopericarditis involves inflammation of both the heart muscle (myocardium) and the pericardium, and can be caused by infectious agents, thus falling under the broader category of infectious myocarditis.
Acute myocarditis refers to the sudden onset of inflammation of the heart muscle, which can be caused by infectious agents, making it a subtype of infectious myocarditis.
